messages:
Anna (arch): Quick sync — we need one coherent pattern for propagating caller/tenant identity across Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private adapters. Spun up a short checklist + 3 proposal sketches below. Looking for clarifying Qs and tradeoff calls before I turn this into an RFC.

Anna (arch): Problem: when a request enters Hosted it has an auth token + tenant metadata. If we proxy to Dedicated or Private (sidecar or mesh) we need to preserve identity for: billing, per-tenant quotas, audit logs, and policy evaluation. But we must avoid leaking customer secrets or creating a hard coupling to control plane KMS.

Anna (arch): Proposal sketches (high level):
1) Forwarding (opaque header): Hosted forwards original token in `X-Redwood-Forwarded-Token` to Dedicated/Private adapter. Adapter validates with control plane on first use, caches short-lived verdicts.
   - Pros: simple, minimal change to adapters
   - Cons: surfaces tokens across boundaries, harder for on-prem where token exchange is undesired

2) Delegated credential exchange (recommended): Hosted exchanges original token for a short-lived adapter-bound credential via control-plane token broker (`/v1/broker/exchange`). Adapter receives `X-Redwood-Delegated` and uses it to reconstruct tenant context locally. Broker issues tight TTL and audience.
   - Pros: limited blast radius, supports per-deployment policies, aligns with KMS/HSM flows
   - Cons: requires token-broker implementation and network calls on cold start

3) Mutual attestation + mTLS identity (sidecar-first): Use mTLS with tenant-labeled service identities (SPIFFE-like). Hosted and adapter perform mutual TLS and exchange tenant bindings in secured metadata.
   - Pros: strong cryptographic binding, minimal token handling
   - Cons: heavy infra, tricky for hosted multi-tenant pools and for customers who cannot share certs in Private

Anna (arch): Implementation checklist I propose for the RFC:
- Acceptance: end-to-end tenant attribution for billing and audit in all modes
- Security: no long-lived customer token stored in adapters; broker-issued creds TTL <= 5m
- Operational: clear metrics (auth failures, broker latency) and fallback path
- Backcompat: adapters accept both `X-Redwood-Forwarded-Token` (deprecated) and `X-Redwood-Delegated`

Suman: Quick q — how do we handle offline/private air-gapped where control-plane cannot be reached for token exchange? We still need audit and tenant mapping.

Anna (arch): Good point. For Private/air-gapped we fall back to local credential bootstrapping: operator supplies a signed binding manifest (signed by customer KMS/HSM or Redwood proxy) that maps local service identity -> tenants. Brokerless flow: manifest rotated via operator.

AJ: FYI: forwarding raw tokens is a non-starter for some enterprise customers. They flagged that in last week's onboarding (GDPR + contractual). Delegated flow is the only acceptable default for sales-facing tenants.

Marco: From runtime perf side — broker exchange adds latency on cold tenant first request. We should implement an async prefetch/hint: when routing decision chooses Dedicated pool, pre-warm delegated creds for top N tenants based on recent traffic.

Olivia: On audit logs: we need canonical tenant-id and canonical principal (actor) in every log line across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Suggest header `X-Redwood-Tenant: <tenant-id>` and `X-Redwood-Principal: <email|service>` (populated after broker validation). These must be redacted in public traces.

Anna (arch): Example delegated exchange (sketch):
```
POST /v1/broker/exchange
Auth: Bearer <hosted-token>
Body: {"audience":"adapter:dedicated:pool-12","ttl":"300"}
-> 200 {"delegated":"ey..short..jwt","tenant":"redwood-acme"}
```
Adapter uses `delegated` to build local context and emits `X-Redwood-Tenant` and `X-Redwood-Principal` to logs.

Suman: For manifest fallback in Private: how do we rotate? Are we doing operator-tools to push new signed manifests? Could be a separate rotation endpoint on the adapter.

Anna (arch): Yes — operator pushes signed manifests via controlchannel or via local S3/manifest store. Rotation windows must be configurable; default 24h rotate-check.

Marco: Operational hazards: if broker is down, ensure adapters reject only if strict mode; default should be soft-fail to previously-cached mapping for N minutes to avoid outage. But soft-fail must be logged and counted.

Olivia: Also add requirement: adapters must scrub tokens from crash dumps and stack traces. We had a near miss last quarter where a forwarded header ended up in a debug dump.

AJ: Can we make the broker issue delegation tokens that are audience-restricted to adapter instance IDs? That way a leaked token is useless outside that adapter.

Anna (arch): Yes — that's the idea. Delegation token includes `aud`=adapter-id and `iss`=broker. TTL short. Adapter must validate `aud` and `iss` and check signature via control-plane public key (rotateable).

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-01-12T15:04:01Z started by Marco — auth-broker-v0.1 image -> staging

Marco: I'll prototype a broker exchange shim and an adapter validation lib. Will also add prefetch support and metrics (exchange_latency, exchange_failures, cached_miss_count). ETA: mock by EOD Friday.

Anna (arch): Great. Action items: Marco prototype + demo; Suman & Olivia draft operator manifest format and rotation API; AJ collect sales/legal constraints to pin acceptance criteria; I'll draft RFC from these notes and include the checklist above.

Olivia: One more: add a privacy-preserving audit option where tenant->principal mapping is hashed with a salt per-day so external leak still can't map user emails.

Anna (arch): Noted. Thanks all. Will post RFC draft in #architecture next Tuesday and tag reviewers. :thumbsup:
